review.scope_note: Only formal Pass 1 SARIF codeFlows reviewed. diagnostics queries and CodeQL built-in security query results were NOT counted as formal TP.
review.independence_note: PyVul ground truth, fix commits, and CVE descriptions were not read for the per-alert triage; the commit snippet supplied in the task prompt was used only for the separate real-vulnerability match analysis (task 2).

context.authentication: mindsdb/utilities/config.py:100 'http_auth_enabled': False by default; PUT /api/files/<name>, PUT /api/handlers/byom/<name>, PUT /api/config/integrations/<name> and POST /api/sql/query are unauthenticated on a default install (start.py before_request only enforces basic auth when enabled).
context.sanitizer_inventory: No safe_join / secure_filename / os.path.normpath / os.path.realpath usage anywhere in mindsdb/api or mindsdb/interfaces (grep verified). os.path.join discards the temp base when the second argument is absolute (file.py:122/129, handlers.py:129); pathlib joinpath appends '..' segments unresolved (file_controller.py:98).
context.primary_taint_origin: PUT /api/files/<name> multipart parsing: python-multipart callbacks on_field (file.py:42-45, field_name/value fully client-controlled) and on_file (file.py:49-52, file_name with UPLOAD_KEEP_FILENAME=True). A form field literally named 'file' or 'name'/'source_type'/'source'/'original_file_name' is pure attacker string input; request.json (file.py:80) is equally attacker-controlled in the non-multipart branch.

allowed_roots.file_py_put: implied allowed root = tempfile.mkdtemp('mindsdb_file_') dir; NEVER enforced: os.path.join(temp_dir_path, data['file']) at file.py:122/129 has no post-join containment check.
allowed_roots.file_controller_save_file: implied allowed root = <content>/file/file_{company_id}_{id}/; store_file_path is server-generated, but the leaf file_name (from original_file_name form field) is joined unchecked at file_controller.py:98; Path(file_path).name barrier at line 71 applies only in the file_name-is-None branch.
allowed_roots.handlers_py_byom: implied allowed root = temp_dir_path; join at handlers.py:129 unchecked.
allowed_roots.config_py_integration: allowed root = temp_dir; ENFORCED by resolve()+parents containment at config.py:133-136.
allowed_roots.integrations_add: no allowed root; raw arg_value used by shutil.copy at integrations.py:68 before the Path(arg_value).name baselining at line 69.

checklist_answers.1_source_is_attacker_controlled: Yes for 9/10 findings: multipart callback field names/values and uploaded file_name (file.py:42-52), plus request.json on the same routes, are raw client input. For A10 the source is the connection_args parameter of IntegrationController.add, fed from request.json['params']/request.form (config.py:121-122) and from SQL CREATE DATABASE ... PARAMETERS / Mongo-MySQL wire protocols.
checklist_answers.2_source_reaches_file_access: Yes for 9/10: verified hop-by-hop in real source. os.path.join at file.py:129 propagates the tainted segment; the dynamic receiver call ca.file_controller.save_file(mindsdb_file_name, file_path, file_name=original_file_name) at file.py:149 reaches file_controller.py:55 parameter, then _handle_source (line 75) -> file_handler.py:98/100 -> _get_data_io:142 -> open:158, and shutil.move at file_controller.py:100. No async boundary or filename transform exists on these paths.
checklist_answers.3_sink_is_sensitive_operation: Yes for all 10 sinks are real file operations (open 'wb'/'rb', ZipFile/tarfile.open, os.remove/os.unlink, shutil.move/copy, werkzeug file.save). A1 (config.py:137 file.save) is a real write but is guarded (see 6).
checklist_answers.4_allowed_root_escape: Yes for 9 findings: absolute second argument to os.path.join discards temp_dir; '..' segments escape the implied temp/content roots; no declared allowlist of filenames exists. A1 cannot escape (containment check).
checklist_answers.5_traversal_vectors: Absolute paths and '..' both work: os.path.join('/tmp/x', 'C:/evil' or '/etc/evil') -> absolute wins; join('..','..') segments survive until OS resolution. Percent-decoding/URL decoding is irrelevant (values arrive already-decoded from multipart/JSON); no double-decoding step exists; symlink following is default (open/shutil) but not required for exploitation.
checklist_answers.6_effective_barriers: Only one effective barrier found: config.py:132-136 - file_path = temp_dir_path.joinpath(file_name).resolve(); if temp_dir_path not in file_path.parents: raise - executed BEFORE file.save at line 137, blocks absolute names and '..' escape (resolve collapses them), fails closed when mkdtemp path itself contains symlinks. file_controller.py:71 Path(file_path).name and integrations.py:69 Path(arg_value).name are effective basename barriers but only apply on their respective branches/after the sink (line 69 runs after the copy on line 68, and line 71 only when file_name is None).
checklist_answers.7_overcredited_barriers: None of the FP patterns applies here in the reverse direction: the report did NOT treat Path.resolve/normpath/startsWith/auth as protection; if anything, resolve() at config.py:133-136 IS part of a genuinely sufficient check (combined with the parents containment and the pre-save ordering), so A1 is a true FP, not an overcredited barrier.
checklist_answers.8_static_service_test_unreachable: No. All 9 TP flows are on live HTTP request handlers of the mindsdb server, reachable by an unauthenticated client on a default install. No test code, no fixed constants as the tainted value.
checklist_answers.9_overgeneralization_fp: One FP from branch-insensitive modeling: A1 (config.py:137) - the taint flow is real but the guarding containment check at 133-136 is branch-sensitive, so the query reports it; the report itself notes K100 was expected to be filtered by the Step 6 explicit-containment heuristic but the filter did not fire ('no explicit FP/TP heuristic matched'). No database coverage or wrong-diagnostic contamination observed.
checklist_answers.10_contamination_of_pass1_results: None. All 10 SARIF results carry ruleId py/augur/mindsdb/pass1-path-traversal from the single custom query; no CodeQL built-in query IDs (e.g. py/path-injection) and no diagnostics results are present in results/pass1.sarif.

sink.operation: werkzeug FileStorage.save(file_path) - writes uploaded file bytes to disk

findings.attacker_controlled_input: multipart filename of a file part on PUT /api/config/integrations/<name>
findings.barrier_evidence: config.py:134 resolve() normalizes '..' and symlinks; config.py:135-136 'if temp_dir_path not in file_path.parents: raise Exception' - strict ancestor-containment check on the RESOLVED path, executed BEFORE the sink at 137. Absolute filename -> joinpath yields the absolute path -> parents do not contain temp_dir_path -> raise. '../..' chains collapse at resolve -> escape detected -> raise. Check fails closed (over-blocks) when the mkdtemp path itself traverses a symlink, never under-blocks.
findings.preconditions: attacker must reach the route (unauthenticated by default) - but the guard rejects every escaping filename.
findings.rationale: Real source and real write sink, but a genuinely sufficient, correctly ordered containment check (resolve + strict parents containment) blocks all absolute and relative traversal before file.save. This is the exact FP class the query notes predicted for K100; the Step 6 filter failed to remove it, so it must be triaged out manually.

sink.operation: open(file_path, 'wb') + f.write(chunk) - writes remote URL content to attacker-chosen path

sources: (also request.json file.py:80, not labeled as source but equally attacker-controlled)
findings.taint_flow: multipart form fields -> data dict (42-45/49-52) -> data['name'] (91, URL branch) -> os.path.join(temp_dir_path, data['file']) (122) -> open(file_path, 'wb') (123)
findings.attacker_controlled_input: form/JSON fields source_type='url', source=<attacker URL>, name=<target path>
findings.barrier_evidence: none. is_cloud size check (93-114) is cloud-only and not a path check; no validation of data['name'] anywhere.
findings.preconditions: data.get('source_type') == 'url' (attacker-supplied field); remote URL must return HTTP 200. Local (non-cloud) installs skip the size check entirely.
findings.actual_impact: arbitrary file WRITE with content fully controlled by the attacker (content is whatever their URL serves), as the mindsdb process user - e.g. overwrite ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, cron files, or mindsdb's own config/static files. os.path.join discards temp_dir_path when data['name'] is absolute; '..' segments escape.
findings.rationale: Source, flow, and sink all verified line-by-line; no barrier; unauthenticated route by default. This is a genuine, exploitable arbitrary-file-write path traversal that the reviewed commit (4419b0f) did NOT fix - code_after keeps open(..., 'wb') unchanged.

sink.operation: zipfile.ZipFile(file_path) - opens attacker-pathed archive for reading (followed by extractall at 134)

sources: multipart callbacks file.py:42-52 (data['file'] from a form field named 'file' or the uploaded file_name)
findings.taint_flow: data['file'] -> os.path.join(temp_dir_path, data['file']) (129) -> lp check (130-131) -> zipfile.ZipFile(file_path) (133)
findings.attacker_controlled_input: data['file'] string: absolute path or '..'-relative path ending in .zip
findings.barrier_evidence: none between line 129 and 133. The 'endswith .zip' branch condition is attacker-satisfied by naming.
findings.preconditions: target path must end with .zip (lowercased check) and be a readable zip archive; full exfiltration additionally requires exactly one member (140) parseable as csv/json/xlsx/parquet (file_handler.py:129).
findings.actual_impact: arbitrary file READ of any existing .zip on the server: its single data member is extracted, stored via save_file, and becomes SELECTable through the files database; os.remove at 138 then deletes the original. Separately, extractall at 134 with unchecked member names is a real zip-slip write (not the reported taint flow, and NOT fixed by commit 4419b0f which only patched the tar branch).
findings.rationale: Taint chain verified; sink performs a real read of an attacker-influenced path outside any allowed root. Confidence moderated by the .zip-suffix and archive-validity preconditions, but a text file renamed .zip is not needed - any genuine zip works, and arbitrary delete (A5) shares the same chain.

sink.operation: tarfile.open(file_path) - opens attacker-pathed tar.gz for reading; its with-body calls f.extractall(temp_dir_path) at line 137 (the exact line fixed by commit 4419b0f)

sources: multipart callbacks file.py:42-52; URL branch writes to join(temp_dir_path, data['name']) at 122 first
findings.barrier_evidence: none. Post-extraction checks (139-147: single-file, isfile) run after the extraction and do not constrain the archive-open path.
findings.preconditions: target must be a valid .tar.gz at the attacker-chosen path for the read/delete impact; the TarSlip write impact (line 137) only needs the attacker to supply their own malicious tarball, which they control end-to-end.
findings.actual_impact: Two distinct real issues: (a) reported flow - arbitrary read/delete of an existing .tar.gz; (b) the statement this alert points into - f.extractall(temp_dir_path) with unvalidated member names is CVE-2007-4559 TarSlip (arbitrary file write via member names like '../../x'), which is exactly what commit 4419b0f fixed with safe_extract.
findings.rationale: Verified taint chain into a real archive read on an escaping path. Additionally this alert's sink line (136) is the direct precursor of the patched line 137 - see real_vulnerability_match for why this counts as an adjacent hit on the CVE rather than a direct detection of its member-name mechanism.

findings.barrier_evidence: none before the remove; the preceding extractall must succeed, which doubles as an existence/validity check.
findings.preconditions: the deletion target must be an openable .zip/.tar.gz archive (the code extracts it first, then removes it).
findings.actual_impact: arbitrary file DELETE of any existing archive path reachable by the process user (destructive, and combined with A3/A4 a read-then-delete primitive).
findings.rationale: Chain verified with no barrier; impact constrained to archive-suffixed files, hence slightly lower confidence, but the constraint is fully attacker-satisfiable against any real zip/tar on disk.

sink.operation: shutil.move(file_path, str(source)) argument 0 - reads and removes the source file, moving it into the content store

sources: multipart callbacks file.py:42-52 via save_file call at file.py:149
findings.taint_flow: data['file'] -> join (129) -> ca.file_controller.save_file(mindsdb_file_name, file_path, file_name=original_file_name) (149) -> save_file param file_path (file_controller.py:55) -> FileHandler._handle_source(file_path) (75) -> shutil.move(file_path, ...) (100 arg0)
findings.attacker_controlled_input: data['file'] path segment from the upload route
findings.allowed_root: temp_dir_path at the caller; content/file/file_{company}_{id}/ at the sink
findings.barrier_evidence: none on this argument: the Path(file_path).name barrier at line 71 applies to file_name (the other parameter) only when it is None, never to file_path.
findings.preconditions: _handle_source at line 75 must parse the file (any text file parses as CSV via pd.read_csv), so most existing files qualify; the archive branch (131) must not have fired, or data['file'] must not be archive-suffixed.
findings.actual_impact: arbitrary file MOVE: the file at the attacker-chosen path is read, then removed from its original location and placed into the mindsdb content store, after which it is queryable - a read + destructive-relocate primitive.
findings.rationale: The dynamic-receiver call bridge (file.py:149 -> file_controller.py:55) is backed by real source; no validation on file_path anywhere in save_file; both the read (via A8) and the move/delete are confirmed.

sink.operation: shutil.move(file_path, str(source)) argument 1 - destination path of the move

sources: S050 file.py:44 field.value - the original_file_name form field
findings.taint_flow: original_file_name = data.get('original_file_name') (file.py:127) -> save_file(file_name=original_file_name) keyword (149) -> file_name param (file_controller.py:55) -> file_dir.joinpath(file_name) (98) -> source -> str(source) -> shutil.move arg1 (100)
findings.barrier_evidence: Path(file_path).name at line 71 applies ONLY when file_name is None (branch-dependent); when the attacker supplies original_file_name, the raw value reaches joinpath. pathlib joinpath does not reject '..' segments - Path(file_dir).joinpath('../../x') moves to the resolved outside path.
findings.preconditions: attacker supplies original_file_name; the moved source (file_path) must be parseable per _handle_source.
findings.actual_impact: arbitrary file WRITE destination: the uploaded temp file (or the arbitrary source from A6) is moved to an attacker-chosen path outside the content root (e.g. overwrite a startup .py or config file), combined with removing the source.
findings.rationale: The keyword-argument bridge (original_file_name -> file_name) matches the real call at file.py:149; the only barrier is branch-gated off by supplying the very field under attack; joinpath offers no containment.

sink.operation: open(file_path, 'rb') + fp.read() - reads the full contents of the attacker-pathed file

findings.taint_flow: data['file'] -> join (129) -> save_file (149) -> file_controller.py:55 -> _handle_source(file_path) (75) -> file_handler.py:98/100 -> _get_data_io(file_path) (142) -> open(file_path, 'rb') (158)
findings.preconditions: the target file must be parseable by _handle_source as parquet/csv/xlsx/json - any plain-text file parses as CSV with pd.read_csv, so this is a weak constraint; non-parsing files still get moved by A6.
findings.actual_impact: arbitrary file READ with exfiltration: file contents become the dataframe whose column names and row count are persisted to the DB (file_controller.py:77-94) and returned by GET /api/files; after the move the whole content is SELECTable via SQL (file_handler.py:78-86 query path uses the same stored file).
findings.rationale: Longest verified chain (13 steps), every hop present in real source, no barrier, and the read content has a concrete exfiltration channel through the files API/SQL.

sources: S054/S060 handlers.py:96-99 BYOM on_file file_name; also request.json at handlers.py:127
findings.taint_flow: data['file'] (98/127) -> os.path.join(temp_dir_path, data['file']) (129) -> connection_args['model_code'] (131-132) -> ca.integration_controller.add(name, 'byom', connection_args) (134) -> os.unlink(file_path) (136)
findings.attacker_controlled_input: data['file'] string (multipart filename, a form field named 'file', or JSON field)
findings.barrier_evidence: none on the join. integrations.py:69 Path(arg_value).name basenames only the stored connection_args copy, not the local file_path used by unlink.
findings.preconditions: add() at line 134 must return normally: engine 'byom' must be registered and model_code is an ARG_TYPE.PATH connection arg (byom_handler.py:111-115), so shutil.copy(arg_value, files_dir) at integrations.py:68 must succeed - i.e. the deletion target must exist. Since the point of the delete is an existing file, the precondition is satisfied exactly when the attack is meaningful.
findings.actual_impact: arbitrary file DELETE of any existing file (no archive-suffix constraint on this route, unlike A5); via the multipart filename the python-multipart parser itself additionally writes the upload to the escaped path (UPLOAD_KEEP_FILENAME, no filename sanitization in the repo).
findings.rationale: Chain verified; the only gating is add() succeeding, which requires the target to exist and byom handler metadata to be loadable - both realistic on a default install. Confidence slightly reduced by that gating.

sink.operation: shutil.copy(arg_value, files_dir) - reads the raw attacker-supplied path and copies it into a temp dir that is then persisted (FileStorage.add + push, integrations.py:73-80)

sources: S013 integrations.py:45 connection_args parameter - fed by config.py:121-122 request.json['params']/request.form on PUT /api/config/integrations/<name> (config.py:161 add(name, engine, params)), by SQL CREATE DATABASE ... PARAMETERS, and by Mongo/MySQL wire protocols
findings.taint_flow: connection_args (45) -> items loop (61) -> arg_value where arg_name has ARG_TYPE.PATH (62-65) -> shutil.copy(arg_value, files_dir) (68); Path(arg_value).name baselining at 69 happens AFTER the copy
findings.attacker_controlled_input: value of any PATH-typed connection arg for the chosen engine
findings.allowed_root: none - raw value used before any normalization
findings.barrier_evidence: the only barrier (Path(arg_value).name, line 69) executes after the sink, so it sanitizes the stored copy but not the file access at line 68.
findings.preconditions: the chosen engine must declare a PATH-typed connection arg - verified present for bigquery (service_account_keys), byom (model_code), cassandra/scylla (secure_connection bundle path), matrixone/mysql (ssl cert/key paths), sqlite (db_file); the target file must exist (shutil.copy raises otherwise); SQL PARAMETERS values additionally require the SQL parse boundary that the S013 label declared.
findings.actual_impact: arbitrary file READ/copy: the file's contents are duplicated into mindsdb's persistent storage (local content dir or S3 per config) and the copy is subsequently used by the handler - for byom the copied model_code is later loaded as model code, and for sqlite the db_file path itself reaches sqlite3.connect (K105, not in the formal alerts). The copy is also a prerequisite enabler for the A9 delete chain.
findings.rationale: Source boundary (S013) and sink are real code with the barrier provably ordered after the sink; PATH-typed args exist on many engines. Confidence moderated by the engine-choice and file-existence preconditions and by the SQL-side boundary relying on the declared S013 parameter node rather than a parsed HTTP expression.

real_vulnerability_match.commit_message: Use safe extract to prevent CVE-2007-4559 bug
real_vulnerability_match.vulnerability: TarSlip / CVE-2007-4559 in File.put (mindsdb/api/http/namespaces/file.py): the tar.gz branch opens an attacker-supplied (URL-retrieved or uploaded) archive and calls f.extractall(temp_dir_path) at line 137 with no member-name validation; archive member names containing '../' write files outside temp_dir_path - arbitrary file write. The fix replaces only the tar-branch extractall with safe_extract(f, temp_dir_path); the zip branch at lines 133-134 (zipfile extractall) remains extractall in code_after.
real_vulnerability_match.source_version_match: The mindsdb_vuln source tree matches the commit's code_before exactly for File.put (verified line-by-line, tar extractall at file.py:135-137).
real_vulnerability_match.direct_hit_evidence: No formal Pass 1 result sinks at file.py:134/137 (the extractall calls). extractall's argument 0 is the constant temp_dir_path, so no tainted string flows into it; labels K097/K098 (extractall sinks, classified tp in labels.json) produced no SARIF results. The TarSlip traversal payload lives in the archive CONTENT (member names), which string taint tracking does not model - the query generation notes themselves acknowledge this ('zip-slip 成员名不是字符串污点，实际由归档打开 sink 承检').
real_vulnerability_match.adjacent_hit_evidence: A4's sink is tarfile.open(file_path) at file.py:136 - the 'with' statement whose body is the patched extractall at 137, driven by the same attacker-controlled data['file'] input; A3 (133, zip branch) and A5 (138, os.remove in the same block) complete the coverage of the vulnerable archive-handling block. An analyst triaging these alerts lands directly on the CVE site.
real_vulnerability_match.additional_real_bugs_hit: The alert set independently confirms real path traversals in the same function that commit 4419b0f did NOT fix: A2 (file.py:123 open(...,'wb') - arbitrary file write with URL-controlled content, still present in code_after), A5/A9 (arbitrary delete), A6/A7/A8 (arbitrary read/move/write-destination via save_file), A10 (arbitrary read via PATH connection args).
real_vulnerability_match.verdict: 邻近命中（adjacent hit）: the formal alerts hit the same vulnerable function, same attack surface, and same input as the commit's CVE, and they certify 9 real path-traversal findings - but the exact CVE-2007-4559 mechanism (extractall member-name escape) is not itself a formal taint path, because its payload is archive content rather than a tainted path string. The alert at file.py:136 points one line away from the patched line 137.

overall_conclusion: CodeQL analysis succeeded and 10 formal Pass 1 path-traversal alerts fired. Independent re-review of every codeFlow against real source confirms 9 likely_tp (arbitrary write at file.py:123, archive read at 133/136, arbitrary delete at 138 and handlers.py:136, arbitrary move/read at file_controller.py:100 arg0/arg1, arbitrary read at file_handler.py:158, arbitrary copy at integrations.py:68) and 1 likely_fp (config.py:137, protected by a genuine resolve+parents containment check that the Step 6 filter failed to suppress). No diagnostics or built-in query results contaminated the formal set. Relative to the supplied real vulnerability (TarSlip at file.py:137, commit 4419b0f): adjacent hit only - same block, same input, but the extractall member-name mechanism produced no formal taint result; the alerts instead certify several other real, unfixed traversals in the same function.
limitations: python-multipart library internals (whether the parser itself sanitizes the kept filename when writing to UPLOAD_DIR) were not verified against the vendored library source; the multipart-field and request.json branches make the conclusions independent of that behavior.
Exploit preconditions (file existence, parseability, engine PATH-arg availability, is_cloud settings) were assessed from project source only; no runtime verification was performed.

The A10 SQL-side reachability relies on the S013 parameter-boundary label declared in labels.json; the intra-DB flow from parse_sql text to the connection_args value is opaque to dataflow and was accepted as a declared boundary.
